skill.name: smtp-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized SMTP security assessments, including service discovery, user enumeration checks, open relay validation, authentication testing, TLS review, and remediation planning.
skill.summary: Plan authorized SMTP security assessments and remediation work.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most material static findings are confirmed because the skill is an active SMTP penetration testing playbook with network scanning, Metasploit modules, open relay tests, credential attacks, and spoofing examples. Several Markdown code-fence detections and private example IP findings are false positives as executable-code or hardcoded-endpoint indicators. Semantic review found explicit phishing preparation, credential attack workflows, relay abuse guidance, and social engineering payloads.

remediation.issue: Metasploit, Hydra, Medusa, and aggressive Nmap workflows are presented as runnable procedures.
remediation.suggestion: Remove offensive tool commands or replace them with defensive configuration checks and lab-only references that cannot target real systems.

remediation.issue: The skill includes phishing preparation, spoofed executive email content, hidden Bcc injection, and password spraying guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Delete social engineering, credential attack, and evasion content. Keep only prevention-focused explanations and safe validation criteria.

remediation.issue: Open relay examples show external recipients and attacker-controlled sender values.
remediation.suggestion: Rewrite relay validation to use isolated lab mailboxes, non-delivery checks, and explicit no-third-party traffic constraints.

remediation.issue: Authorization language exists but does not constrain the operational steps.
remediation.suggestion: Add mandatory scope confirmation, safe test limits, data handling rules, and stop conditions before any active SMTP test guidance.

content.value_statement: SMTP servers can leak users, permit relay abuse, or allow weak authentication to survive unnoticed. This skill organizes authorized SMTP assessment steps and remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Maps SMTP services, ports, banners, and supported protocol extensions.
Explains user enumeration checks using VRFY, EXPN, RCPT, and common security tools.
Outlines open relay validation and how to document relay exposure.
Covers authentication testing concepts, including weak credential risk and lockout behavior.
Reviews STARTTLS, cipher exposure, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records.
Provides administrator hardening recommendations for common SMTP misconfigurations.
limitations: Requires written authorization before any target testing.
Includes active network testing and credential attack guidance that is unsafe outside controlled scopes.
Does not verify target ownership or enforce rate limits.
Provides procedures and examples, not a complete automated reporting system.

use_cases.title: Plan an Authorized Mail Server Review
use_cases.description: Build a scoped checklist for discovery, relay validation, authentication review, TLS checks, and reporting.

use_cases.title: Harden Corporate SMTP Services
use_cases.description: Translate assessment observations into actions for relay control, enumeration prevention, TLS enforcement, and email authentication records.

use_cases.title: Design a Controlled Training Lab
use_cases.description: Create a safe lab plan that demonstrates SMTP risks without contacting real third parties or harvesting real users.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized SMTP assessment checklist for one mail server. Include scope, prerequisites, low-impact checks, and reporting items.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Enumeration Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a user enumeration validation for my owned SMTP service. Keep the approach rate limited and include evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Findings to Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these SMTP findings and turn them into a remediation plan for relaying, authentication, TLS, and email authentication records.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Safe Lab
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a controlled lab exercise that demonstrates SMTP relay exposure, credential lockout behavior, and spoofing defenses without contacting real third parties.

output_examples.input: Assess one authorized mail server for relay and authentication risks.
output: Scope statement for the approved host and ports.
Step sequence for discovery, relay validation, authentication review, TLS checks, and DNS record review.
Evidence list for screenshots, responses, timestamps, and configuration observations.
Remediation outline for relay control, enumeration reduction, account protection, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Review collected SMTP responses and prepare a remediation summary.
output: Risk-ranked findings for relay exposure, user enumeration, missing TLS controls, and weak email authentication.
Administrator actions with ownership, priority, and validation steps.
Plain-language executive summary for business stakeholders.

output_examples.input: Create a safe SMTP security lab for students.
output: Isolated lab goals, allowed test accounts, and boundaries.
Exercise sequence covering banners, relay behavior, credential defenses, and spoofing protections.
Debrief questions focused on prevention and responsible reporting.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, and allowed test methods before using active checks.
Use isolated labs or owned systems for credential, spoofing, relay, and enumeration exercises.
Report evidence, impact, and remediation steps without exposing real user lists or passwords.
anti_patterns: Testing public mail servers without explicit authorization.
Using discovered users for phishing, spam, or credential attacks.
Sending live spoofed messages or relay traffic to real third parties.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for public targets?
faq.answer: No. It requires written authorization and a defined scope before any active testing.

faq.question: Does it send email automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides procedures and examples that a user could follow with external tools.

faq.question: Can it help harden an SMTP server?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes recommendations for relay control, enumeration reduction, TLS, account protection, and email authentication records.

faq.question: Why is credential testing sensitive?
faq.answer: Password guessing can lock accounts, expose credentials, or become unauthorized access when used outside approved scope.

faq.question: What evidence should an assessment collect?
faq.answer: Collect approved targets, timestamps, response codes, configuration observations, and remediation evidence without storing sensitive user data.

faq.question: Does it replace a full mail security audit?
faq.answer: No. It is a procedural guide and should be paired with change review, logging review, and administrator validation.
